questions.question: The distance between the pole and focus of a concave mirror is 30 { cm} . A real and inverted image is formed by this mirror on a screen at 40 { cm} from the pole of this mirror. What will be the object distance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**- 120 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **focal length (f)** of a **concave mirror** is always considered **negative**. In this problem, the distance between the **pole** and **focus** is given as **30 cm**, so **f = -30 cm**.
 
• A **real and inverted image** is formed on a screen, which means the image is formed in front of the mirror. Therefore, the **image distance (v)** is also **negative**. Given the image is at **40 cm**, we have **v = -40 cm**.
 
• The **Mirror Formula** relates the focal length, image distance, and object distance: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**. ***Hence, the formula application is essential for this calculation.***
 
• Substituting the known values into the formula: **1/(-30) = 1/(-40) + 1/u**. Rearranging for the **object distance (u)**, we get **1/u = -1/30 - (-1/40)**, which simplifies to **1/u = -1/30 + 1/40**.
 
• Finding the common denominator (120): **1/u = (-4 + 3) / 120 = -1 / 120**. Therefore, **u = -120 cm**. The negative sign indicates that the **object** is placed **120 cm** in front of the mirror. ***Hence, the statement regarding the object distance being -120 cm is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:** A **concave mirror**, or converging mirror, has a reflecting surface that is recessed inward. It reflects light inward to one **focal point**. These mirrors are used to focus light and are common in **telescopes**, **shaving mirrors**, and **headlights**.
 
• **Nature of Images:**
 
 
• If the object is placed beyond the **Center of Curvature (C)**, the image is **real, inverted**, and **diminished**.
 
• If the object is between **C** and **Focus (F)**, the image is **real, inverted**, and **magnified**.
 
• If the object is placed between the **Pole (P)** and **F**, the image is **virtual, erect**, and **magnified**.
 
 
 
• **Cartesian Sign Convention:**
 
 
• The **object** is always placed to the **left** of the mirror, making **u** always **negative**.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of incident light are **positive**, and those opposite are **negative**.
 
• The **height** measured upwards from the **principal axis** is **positive**, while downwards is **negative**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object. It is also given by the formula **m = -v/u**. For **real images**, **m** is **negative**, and for **virtual images**, **m** is **positive**.
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):** The distance from the **pole** to the **center of curvature**. There is a specific relationship where **R = 2f**. In this problem, the radius of curvature would be **60 cm**.
 
• **Real vs Virtual Image:** A **real image** can be obtained on a **screen** because the light rays actually intersect. A **virtual image** cannot be obtained on a screen as the light rays only appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror.
 
• The **unit** of measurement must remain consistent throughout the calculation. Since the focal length and image distance were in **cm**, the result for the object distance is also in **cm**.
</ul

questions.question: In which state of matter is the space between particles maximum ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **gaseous state**, the **intermolecular space** between the particles is **maximum**. This is because the **intermolecular forces of attraction** between the particles are very weak or almost negligible compared to solids and liquids.
 
• Particles in a **gas** possess very high **kinetic energy**, which causes them to move **randomly** at high speeds in all directions. This rapid motion constantly pushes the particles away from each other, resulting in large empty spaces.
 
• Due to these **maximum spaces**, gases do not have a **definite shape** or a **definite volume**; they expand to fill whatever container they are placed in.
 
• The large distance between particles also makes gases highly **compressible**. For example, **LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas)** and **CNG (Compressed Natural Gas)** are stored by compressing large volumes of gas into small cylinders. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• In contrast, the space between particles is **minimum in solids** because of very strong **cohesive forces** that hold the particles in fixed positions. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• In **liquids**, the space between particles is **intermediate**—more than solids but significantly less than gases. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solid State:**
 
 
• Particles are arranged in a **closely packed** manner, often in a regular **crystal lattice**.
 
• They have a **definite shape**, **distinct boundaries**, and **fixed volumes**.
 
• The **diffusion rate** in solids is extremely low due to the lack of space for particle movement.
 
 
 
• **Liquid State:**
 
 
• Particles have more **freedom of movement** than in solids, allowing liquids to **flow** and change shape.
 
• They have a **fixed volume** but take the shape of the container they occupy.
 
• The **intermolecular force** is strong enough to keep the particles together but not strong enough to keep them in a fixed position.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Theory of Matter:**
 
 
• This theory states that all **matter** is made up of tiny particles that are in **constant motion**.
 
• As the **temperature** increases, the **kinetic energy** of the particles increases, which can lead to a change in the **state of matter** (e.g., melting or evaporation) by increasing the space between particles.
 
 
 
• **Other States of Matter:**
 
 
• **Plasma:** Often considered the **fourth state of matter**, it consists of **super energetic** and **super excited** particles in the form of **ionized gases**. It is found in **stars** and **fluorescent tubes**.
 
• **Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC):** The **fifth state of matter**, formed by cooling a gas of extremely low density to **super-low temperatures** (near **Absolute Zero**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Density:** Usually, the **density** of a substance is **maximum in its solid state** and **minimum in its gaseous state** because density is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by the particles.
 
• **Diffusion:** The **rate of diffusion** is highest in **gases** because the particles move rapidly and there is a lot of **space** between them to mix with other particles.
 
• **Brownian Motion:** This refers to the **zig-zag motion** of particles, which is most observable in **gases** and **liquids** due to the available space for movement.

questions.question: What is the most important condition for successful fragmentation reproduction in Spirogyra?

options.text: Presence of reproductive organs in each fragment
The ability of fragments to form seeds
Each fragment possessing the capability to perform basic life functions
Availability of a fully developed vascular system

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Each fragment possessing the capability to perform basic life functions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spirogyra** is a genus of **filamentous green algae** belonging to the order **Zygnematales**. It is widely known for its characteristic **spiral or helical arrangement** of chloroplasts.
 
• In **Spirogyra**, **asexual reproduction** occurs primarily through a process known as **fragmentation**. In this process, the vegetative body (filament) simply breaks into smaller pieces or fragments upon reaching maturity.
 
• The fundamental condition for successful **fragmentation** is that **each fragment** must contain the necessary cellular machinery to sustain itself. Because **Spirogyra** is a simple multicellular organism, each cell within the filament is relatively **autonomous** and capable of performing **metabolism**, **growth**, and **cell division**.
 
• Once a fragment is separated, it undergoes repeated **mitotic cell divisions** to develop into a full-sized, **new filament**. This allows the organism to multiply rapidly in favorable environmental conditions.
 
• Unlike higher plants, **Spirogyra** does not require specialized **reproductive organs** like flowers or **seeds** for this type of reproduction. As a member of the **Thallophyta** group, it also lacks a **vascular system** (xylem and phloem).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Morphology and Structure**: **Spirogyra** is often called **"water silk"** or **"pond scum"** due to its bright green, slimy appearance. The slipperiness is due to a thick **mucilage coating** on the outer **cell wall**, which protects the filament from epiphytes and pathogens.
 
• **Habitat**: It is typically found in **freshwater** environments such as **ponds**, **lakes**, and slow-moving **streams**. It thrives in clear, stagnant water where sunlight is abundant for **photosynthesis**.
 
• **Sexual Reproduction**: While **fragmentation** is the common asexual method, **Spirogyra** also reproduces sexually through a process called **conjugation**. This involves the fusion of two **non-flagellated gametes** (isogamy), resulting in the formation of a thick-walled **zygospore** that can survive harsh conditions.
 
• **Chloroplasts and Pyrenoids**: The chloroplasts are **ribbon-shaped** and contain small round bodies called **pyrenoids**. These pyrenoids are responsible for the **storage of starch** and the synthesis of proteins.
 
• **Cell Wall Composition**: The cell wall is composed of two distinct layers: an inner layer made of **cellulose** and an outer layer made of **pectose**. The **pectose** layer eventually turns into **pectin** and dissolves in water to form the slimy sheath.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Classification**: It belongs to the **Kingdom Plantae** and the division **Thallophyta**. The name is derived from the **Greek** words "spira" (spiral) and "gyros" (circle).
 
• **Regeneration Capability**: The success of **fragmentation** is a testament to the high **regenerative capacity** of simple multicellular organisms. As long as a fragment contains at least one healthy cell with a **nucleus** and **cytoplasm**, it can regenerate an entire organism.
 
• **Ecological Role**: As a primary producer, **Spirogyra** plays a vital role in **aquatic ecosystems** by producing **oxygen** through **photosynthesis** and serving as a food source for various aquatic insects and small fish.
</ul

questions.question: Which cells in xylem are primarily responsible for the vertical transport of water and minerals in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tracheids and vessels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a complex permanent tissue in **vascular plants** primarily responsible for the conduction of **water and dissolved minerals** from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• **Tracheids** and **vessels** are the two main types of **conducting elements** in the xylem. They are both dead cells at maturity and lack **protoplasm**, creating a hollow path for efficient liquid movement. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• **Tracheids** are elongated, tube-like cells with thick, **lignified walls** and tapering ends. Water moves between tracheids through **pits** in their cell walls. They are found in all vascular plants, including **Pteridophytes** and **Gymnosperms**.
 
• **Vessels** are long, cylindrical structures that result from the fusion of several cells called **vessel members**. These members are interconnected through **perforation plates** in their common walls, allowing for a more streamlined and high-volume vertical transport compared to tracheids.
 
• While **Tracheids** provide a degree of mechanical support, their primary function, alongside **Vessels**, is the **ascent of sap**. Most **Angiosperms** (flowering plants) possess both, whereas vessels are typically absent in most gymnosperms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Xylem Fibres**: These cells have highly thickened walls and obliterated central lumens. Their primary function is to provide **mechanical strength** and structural support to the plant body, rather than active transport. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Xylem Parenchyma**: These are the only **living cells** in the xylem tissue. They are thin-walled and primarily involved in the **storage of food** materials like starch and fats, and the **radial conduction** of water.
 
• **Sieve Tubes**: These are the main conducting elements of the **Phloem**. They are long, tube-like structures arranged longitudinally, responsible for the transport of **organic nutrients** (food) from leaves to other parts. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Companion Cells**: These are specialized parenchymatous cells associated with sieve tube elements in the phloem. They help maintain the **pressure gradient** in the sieve tubes for food transport. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lignification**: The cell walls of tracheids and vessels are heavily impregnated with **lignin**, a complex polymer that provides rigidity and prevents the cells from collapsing under the **negative pressure** (tension) created by **transpiration**.
 
• **Unidirectional Flow**: Unlike the phloem, where transport can be multidirectional, the transport of water and minerals in the xylem is strictly **unidirectional**, moving from **roots to shoots**.
 
• **Ascent of Sap**: The movement of water through tracheids and vessels is driven by physical forces such as **transpiration pull**, **capillary action**, and **root pressure**. **Transpiration pull** is the primary driver in tall trees, pulling water upward through the continuous xylem columns.
</ul

questions.question: The heating effect of electric current is least in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The heating effect of electric current, also known as **Joule heating**, is governed by the formula **H = I²Rt**, where **H** is the heat produced, **I** is the current, **R** is the resistance, and **t** is the time for which the current flows.
 
• According to this law, the amount of heat generated in a conductor is **directly proportional** to its **electrical resistance**. Therefore, a material with lower resistance will produce less heat when the same amount of current passes through it.
 
• **Copper** is known for having very **low electrical resistivity** (approximately **1.68 x 10^-8 Ohm-m** at **20 degrees Celsius**), which makes it an excellent conductor of electricity. Because its resistance is minimal, the **heating effect is least** in copper compared to the other options provided. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Iron** has a significantly higher resistivity (about **1.0 x 10^-7 Ohm-m**) than copper. This means an iron wire will offer more resistance to the flow of electrons and consequently generate more heat than a copper wire of the same dimensions. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**

questions.question: A race car starting from rest accelerates uniformly. If the car covers 22.5 m in the 5th second of its motion, what is the total distance covered at the end of 10 seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**250 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the total distance, we first need to determine the **acceleration** of the race car using the formula for distance covered in the **nth second** of motion.
 
• The formula for the distance covered in the **nth second** is given by: **Sn = u + a/2 (2n - 1)**, where **u** is the **initial velocity**, **a** is the **uniform acceleration**, and **n** is the **time in seconds**.
 
• Given that the car starts from **rest**, the **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**. The car covers **22.5 m** in the **5th second** (n = 5). Substituting these values: **22.5 = 0 + a/2 (2 * 5 - 1)**.
 
• Solving for acceleration: **22.5 = a/2 (9)**, which simplifies to **22.5 = 4.5a**. Therefore, the **acceleration (a)** is **5 m/s²**.
 
• Now, to find the **total distance** covered at the end of **10 seconds**, we use the second equation of motion: **S = ut + 1/2 at²**.
 
• Substituting the known values (u = 0, a = 5, t = 10): **S = (0 * 10) + 1/2 * 5 * (10)²**. This results in **S = 1/2 * 5 * 100**, which equals **250 m**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 250 m.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion:** 
 
 
• These equations describe the behavior of a physical system in terms of its **motion** as a function of **time**. They are valid only when the **acceleration** is **constant** (uniform).
 
• The three primary equations are: **v = u + at**, **S = ut + 1/2 at²**, and **v² = u² + 2aS**.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** 
 
 
• This occurs when the **velocity** of an object changes by an equal amount in every equal **time interval**. In this problem, the race car's acceleration remains **5 m/s²** throughout the **10 seconds**.
 
 
 
• **Initial Velocity (u):** 
 
 
• In physics problems, the phrase **"starting from rest"** is a key indicator that the **initial velocity** is **0**. If an object comes to a **stop**, the **final velocity (v)** becomes **0**.
 
 
 
• **Displacement vs. Distance:** 
 
 
• While often used interchangeably in straight-line motion without a change in direction, **displacement** is a **vector quantity** (shortest path), whereas **distance** is a **scalar quantity** (total path covered).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nth second calculation:** It is important to distinguish between the distance covered **"in 10 seconds"** and the distance covered **"in the 10th second"**. The former is the **cumulative sum** from **0 to 10**, while the latter is only the movement between **second 9** and **second 10**.
 
• **Units:** Always ensure that the units are consistent. In this problem, distance is in **meters (m)** and time is in **seconds (s)**, so the resulting acceleration is in **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• **Linear Relationship:** For an object starting from rest with **uniform acceleration**, the **total distance** covered is directly proportional to the **square of the time** (S ∝ t²).

questions.question: What is the typical oxide used along with aluminium in a thermite reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron (III) oxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **thermite reaction** is a highly **exothermic** chemical reaction between a metal powder and a metal oxide. The most common and typical version involves **Aluminium** powder and **Iron (III) oxide** (**Fe2O3**).
 
• In this process, **Aluminium** acts as a strong **reducing agent** because it has a higher affinity for oxygen than iron. It reduces the **Iron (III) oxide** to produce **molten iron** and **Aluminium oxide** (**Al2O3**).
 
• The reaction is represented by the chemical equation: **Fe2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Fe + Heat**. The heat generated is so intense that the iron produced is in a **liquid (molten) state**.
 
• Because of the production of molten iron, this reaction is extensively used for **welding** broken **railway tracks** and heavy machinery parts on-site where traditional welding is difficult.
 
• While other metal oxides like **Copper oxide** or **Chromium oxide** can technically undergo similar reactions with aluminium, **Iron (III) oxide** is the standard "thermite" component used in industrial and civil engineering applications. ***Hence, the correct answer is Iron (III) oxide.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Discovery:** The thermite process was discovered and patented by the **German** chemist **Hans Goldschmidt** in the year **1893**. It is often referred to as the **Goldschmidt reaction** or the **aluminothermic process**.
 
• **Temperature:** The reaction can reach temperatures of approximately **2500°C** (**4500°F**), which is sufficient to melt almost any metal.
 
• **Ignition:** Thermite is stable at room temperature and requires a very high **activation energy** to start. Typically, a **Magnesium ribbon** or a mixture of **Potassium Permanganate** and **Glycerin** is used as a fuse to provide the initial heat required for ignition.
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Railway Industry:** Used for **Thermite Welding** (or **Exothermic Welding**) to join rails together, ensuring a smooth surface for trains.
 
• **Military:** Used in **incendiary weapons** and grenades to destroy enemy equipment, as the molten iron can melt through thick armor or engine blocks.
 
• **Metallurgy:** Employed in the **reduction of ores** for metals that are difficult to extract using carbon, such as **Chromium** and **Manganese**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Redox Nature:** The thermite reaction is a classic example of a **Redox (Reduction-Oxidation) reaction** and a **displacement reaction**, where a more reactive metal (Aluminium) displaces a less reactive metal (Iron) from its oxide.
 
• **Reactivity Series:** The success of the reaction depends on **Aluminium** being positioned higher than **Iron** in the **reactivity series** of metals.
 
• **Safety:** Due to the extreme temperatures and the fact that it is nearly impossible to extinguish once started (as it carries its own supply of **oxygen** within the metal oxide), it poses significant **fire hazards** and requires specialized safety protocols.
 
• **States of Matter:** The reactants are usually in **powdered form** to increase the **surface area**, ensuring a faster and more consistent reaction rate upon ignition.

questions.question: If the velocity of a car increases from 20 m/s to 40 m/s in 4 seconds, the acceleration of the car is _____.
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**5 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** of an object with respect to **time**.
 
• To find the acceleration in this problem, we use the standard formula: **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, and **t** is the time taken.
 
• Based on the question, the **Initial Velocity (u)** is **20 m/s** and the **Final Velocity (v)** is **40 m/s**.
 
• The **Time interval (t)** given for this change is **4 seconds**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **a = (40 - 20) / 4**. This results in **20 / 4**, which equals **5**.
 
• The unit of velocity is **m/s** and time is **s**, therefore the **SI unit** for acceleration is **m/s²** (meters per second squared). ***Hence, the correct answer is 5 m/s².***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concept of Acceleration:**
 
 
• Acceleration is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• If the velocity of an object increases, the acceleration is **positive** and acts in the direction of motion.
 
• If the velocity of an object decreases, it is known as **deceleration** or **retardation**, and the value is **negative**.
 
• In **uniform circular motion**, even if the speed is constant, the object is accelerating because its **direction** is constantly changing.
 
 
 
• **Velocity and Speed:**
 
 
• **Velocity** is the displacement of an object per unit **time**. It is different from **speed** because speed is a **scalar quantity** and does not account for direction.
 
• The **average velocity** can be calculated by dividing the total **displacement** by the total **time** taken.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**

questions.question: Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for work to be done according to science?

options.text: Only the object moves, even if no force is applied.
A force must act on an object, and the object must be displaced.
Only a force is applied, even if the object does not move.
The object is at rest, and a force is applied.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A force must act on an object, and the object must be displaced**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the field of **Physics**, the term **Work** describes a specific process where energy is transferred. For work to be scientifically recognized as "done," two essential conditions must be simultaneously satisfied: an external **Force** must be applied, and the object must undergo **Displacement** in the direction of the force.
 
• A **force** must act on an object to initiate or change its state of motion. If there is no force, no scientific work can be attributed to an agent. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The object must move through a certain distance, known as **displacement**. If an individual exerts a massive amount of force against a stationary wall and the wall does not move, the displacement is **zero**, and thus no work is done. ***Hence, statement 3 and statement 4 are incorrect.***
 
• The correct scientific condition requires both the presence of an acting **force** and a resulting **displacement**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Furthermore, for work to be non-zero, the force must have a component that is not **perpendicular** to the direction of motion. If the force is applied at **90 degrees** to the displacement, the work done is **zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mathematical Formula**: The amount of work done is calculated using the formula **W = Fs cos θ**, where **W** is work, **F** is the magnitude of the **force**, **s** is the **displacement**, and **θ** is the angle between the force and the displacement vectors.
 
• **SI Unit**: The standard unit of work is the **Joule** (**J**). One Joule is defined as the work done when a force of one **Newton** (**N**) displaces an object by one **meter** (**m**).
 
• **Nature of Quantity**: Work is a **scalar quantity**. While both force and displacement are **vector quantities**, their dot product (work) only has magnitude and no direction.
 
• **Types of Work**:
 
 
• **Positive Work**: When the force and displacement are in the same direction (angle **0°**), such as an object falling under **gravity**.
 
• **Negative Work**: When the force acts opposite to the direction of motion (angle **180°**), such as the force of **friction** acting on a moving vehicle.
 
• **Zero Work**: When there is no displacement, or when the force is perpendicular to the displacement (angle **90°**), such as a satellite orbiting Earth in a **circular path**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This principle states that the net work done on an object is equal to the change in its **Kinetic Energy**. This establishes a direct link between motion and the work performed by forces.
 
• **CGS Unit**: In the **Centimetre-Gram-Second** system, the unit of work is the **Erg**. One **Joule** is equivalent to **10⁷ Ergs**.
 
• **Historical Context**: The concept of work was developed by mathematicians and physicists like **Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis** in the **1820s** to describe the "weight lifted through a height."
 
• **Examples in Daily Life**: Pulling a trolley, lifting a book from the floor, or stretching a spring are all examples where work is done because a **force** results in **displacement**. However, standing still while holding a heavy suitcase is not considered work in physics because the **displacement** is **zero**.

• We use the **Third Equation of Motion**: **v² = u² + 2as**.
 
 
• Substituting the values: **0² = u² + 2(-10)(20)**.
 
• **0 = u² - 400**.
 
• **u² = 400**.
 
• **u = √400 = 20 m/s**.

• The **standard value** of gravity on Earth is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, but for competitive exams and ease of calculation, it is often taken as **10 m/s²**.
 
• It is a **vector quantity** directed towards the center of the Earth.

• When an object is thrown **vertically upwards**, the direction of motion is positive, but **gravity acts downwards**, making **acceleration negative**.

questions.question: What is a colloidal solution?

options.text: Mixture in which particles fully dissolve and settle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heterogeneous mixture with fine particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **colloid** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which one substance consisting of microscopically dispersed **insoluble particles** (the **dispersed phase**) is suspended throughout another substance (the **dispersion medium**).
 
• The **particle size** in a colloidal solution is intermediate between a **true solution** and a **suspension**, generally ranging from **1 nanometer to 1000 nanometers**. These **fine particles** are small enough that they do not settle out upon standing but large enough to scatter light. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• In a **suspension**, the particles are **large** (typically greater than **1000 nm**) and will eventually **settle** due to gravity. Colloids do not settle, which distinguishes them from suspensions. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **colloidal solution** is usually **translucent** or **opaque** because the particles are large enough to scatter light (the **Tyndall effect**). It is not a **transparent** mixture limited only to **gases**; it can involve solids and liquids as well. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• In a **true solution**, the solute particles **fully dissolve** and are molecular or ionic in size (less than **1 nm**). Because colloidal particles are **insoluble** and stay suspended without **settling**, they do not follow the behavior of a true solution or a settling suspension. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

__
 
• **The Tyndall Effect:** This is a defining **feature** of colloidal solutions where a **beam of light** becomes visible as it passes through the mixture. The **fine particles** scatter the light rays, a phenomenon not seen in **true solutions** because their particles are too small.
 
• **Brownian Motion:** Colloidal particles exhibit a continuous, random, zig-zag motion known as **Brownian motion**. This motion is caused by the constant **bombardment** of the dispersed particles by the molecules of the **dispersion medium**, which helps keep the particles in suspension and prevents them from **settling**.
 
• **Classification of Colloids:** Colloids are categorized based on the state of the **dispersed phase** and **dispersion medium**:
 
 
• **Aerosol:** Liquid or solid in gas (e.g., **fog, mist, smoke**).
 
• **Emulsion:** Liquid in liquid (e.g., **milk, face cream, butter**).
 
• **Sol:** Solid in liquid (e.g., **mud, paints, milk of magnesia**).
 
• **Gel:** Liquid in solid (e.g., **jelly, cheese, curd**).
 
• **Foam:** Gas in liquid (e.g., **shaving cream, whipped cream**).
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** The term "colloid" was first coined by the **Scottish scientist Thomas Graham** in **1861**. He derived the name from the **Greek word "kolla,"** meaning **glue**, as many early colloids studied had glue-like properties.
 
• **Stability and Charge:** Colloidal particles often carry an **electric charge** (either positive or negative), which is **uniform** across all particles in a specific colloid. This like-charge creates **repulsion** between particles, preventing them from **aggregating** and contributing to the **stability** of the solution.

• **Filtration:** Unlike suspensions, colloidal particles cannot be separated from the mixture by **ordinary filtration** because they are small enough to pass through the pores of **filter paper**. However, they can be separated using **ultra-filtration** or **centrifugation**.
 
• **Applications:** Colloids are vital in various **industries** and **biological processes**. For **example**, the **blood** in our bodies is a colloidal system. </ul

Fill in the blanks with the correct sequence of organs.

Urine is formed in the _______ → passes through the _______ → stored in the _______ → and finally released through the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kidney → Ureter → Urinary bladder → Urethra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **human excretory system** consists of a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder, and a urethra. Its primary role is to filter out **nitrogenous wastes** and maintain **osmoregulation**.

• **Kidney**: Urine formation starts here through the filtration of blood. The **kidneys** extract waste products such as **urea** and **excess salts** from the bloodstream to form urine.

• **Ureter**: These are long, muscular tubes that carry urine from the **renal pelvis** of each kidney to the urinary bladder. Urine moves through these tubes via **peristalsis**.

• **Urinary bladder**: This is a hollow, muscular sac-like organ that stores urine temporarily. It expands as it fills and sends signals to the **brain** when it needs to be emptied.

• **Urethra**: This is the final canal through which urine is expelled from the body. The process of releasing urine is scientifically known as **micturition**.

• The correct physiological sequence for the passage of urine is **Kidney** (formation) → **Ureter** (conduction) → **Urinary bladder** (storage) → **Urethra** (excretion). ***Hence, the sequence Kidney → Ureter → Urinary bladder → Urethra is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **The Kidneys:**

• Each kidney contains approximately **1 million** functional units called **nephrons**.

• The **nephron** is responsible for three main processes: **glomerular filtration**, **tubular reabsorption**, and **tubular secretion**.

• The kidneys also produce hormones like **erythropoietin**, which stimulates the production of **red blood cells**.

• **The Ureters:**

• These tubes are approximately **25 to 30 cm** in length.

• They enter the bladder at an oblique angle to prevent the **backflow** (reflux) of urine toward the kidneys.

• **The Urinary Bladder:**

• An average adult bladder can hold between **400 ml to 600 ml** of urine before the urge to urinate becomes strong.

• The bladder wall contains a specialized muscle called the **detrusor muscle**, which contracts during urination.

• **The Urethra:**

• In **females**, the urethra is much shorter (about **4 cm**), while in **males**, it is longer (about **20 cm**) and also serves as a passage for **semen**.

• The flow of urine is controlled by internal and external **urethral sphincters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Urine Composition**: Healthy human urine typically consists of about **95% water** and **5% organic/inorganic wastes** like **urea**, **creatinine**, **ammonia**, and **uric acid**.

• **Daily Output**: An average adult human excretes about **1 to 1.5 liters** of urine per **24 hours**, though this varies based on fluid intake and environmental conditions.

questions.question: Herbicides protect crops by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Killing weeds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Herbicides**, also commonly known as **weedkillers**, are a specific type of **pesticide** used to kill or inhibit the growth of **undesired plants**, known as **weeds**.
 
• The primary function of herbicides in agriculture is to eliminate **competition**; weeds compete with **crops** for vital resources such as **water**, **soil nutrients**, **sunlight**, and **spatial area**.
 
• By removing these competitors, herbicides ensure that the **primary crop** receives the maximum available resources, which directly leads to an increase in **crop yield** and overall **quality** of the harvest. ***Hence, the statement "Killing weeds" is correct.***
 
• Herbicides are classified into two main types: **Selective herbicides**, which control specific weed species while leaving the desired crop relatively unharmed, and **Non-selective herbicides** (often called **total weedkillers**), which kill all plant material they contact.
 
• The application of these chemicals is a critical component of **modern industrial agriculture**, allowing for **large-scale monoculture** and reducing the need for **manual weeding** or intensive **tillage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fungicides:** These are chemical compounds or biological organisms used to kill or inhibit **fungi** or **fungal spores**. Fungal diseases can cause devastating losses in crops like **wheat**, **rice**, and **potatoes** (e.g., **Late Blight**). Common examples include **Bordeaux mixture** and **Sulfur-based** sprays.
 
• **Insecticides:** These are substances used to kill **insects**. They include **ovicides** and **larvicides** used against insect eggs and larvae, respectively. These are used to protect crops from pests like **aphids**, **locusts**, and **bollworms**. A well-known historical example is **DDT**, though many modern versions like **Neonicotinoids** are now more common.
 
• **Bactericides:** These are chemicals used specifically to control **bacterial plant diseases**. While less common than fungicides, they are used to treat conditions like **citrus canker** or **fire blight** in orchards. Many bactericides are **copper-based** or involve **antibiotics** like **streptomycin**.
 
• **Rodenticides:** These are a category of pest control chemicals intended to kill **rodents** (rats and mice) that might consume crops in the field or damage **stored grains** in **warehouses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Modes of Action:** Herbicides work through various biological mechanisms, such as **inhibiting photosynthesis**, disrupting **cell division**, or interfering with the synthesis of **essential amino acids**.
 
• **Timing of Application:** They can be applied as **Pre-planting** (incorporated into the soil before sowing), **Pre-emergence** (applied before the weed or crop sprouts), or **Post-emergence** (applied after the plants are visible).
 
• **Popular Examples:** **2,4-D** is one of the oldest and most widely used selective herbicides in the world, primarily used to control **broadleaf weeds**. **Glyphosate** is a famous non-selective systemic herbicide used extensively in **no-till farming**.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Excessive use of herbicides can lead to **soil degradation**, **water contamination**, and the development of **herbicide-resistant weeds** (often called **superweeds**), which poses a challenge for **sustainable agriculture**.

questions.question: In a longitudinal wave, particle’s motion is ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**parallel to the wave direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **longitudinal wave**, the particles of the medium vibrate or oscillate in a direction that is **parallel** to the direction of energy transport. This means if the wave moves from **left to right**, the particles of the medium oscillate **back and forth** along the same left-to-right axis.
 
• These waves are characterized by the formation of **compressions** and **rarefactions**. **Compressions** are regions where the particles are closest together (high pressure), while **rarefactions** are regions where the particles are farthest apart (low pressure).
 
• A classic example of a longitudinal wave is a **sound wave** traveling through a medium like **air**, **water**, or **steel**. When a sound wave travels, the air molecules move back and forth, creating pressure variations that our ears detect.
 
• Longitudinal waves can propagate through **solids, liquids, and gases**. This is because these waves depend on the **elasticity of volume** of the medium, and all three states of matter possess this property.
 
• In **seismology**, the **P-waves (Primary waves)** generated during an earthquake are longitudinal waves. They are the fastest seismic waves and can travel through both the **liquid outer core** and the **solid mantle** of the Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transverse Waves:** Unlike longitudinal waves, in a **transverse wave**, the particles of the medium move **perpendicular** to the direction of the wave motion. Examples include **light waves**, **radio waves**, and waves produced in a **plucked guitar string**.
 
• **Mechanical Waves:** Both longitudinal and transverse waves (when traveling through a medium) are types of **mechanical waves**. These waves require a **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) for their propagation and cannot travel through a **vacuum**.
 
• **Wave Parameters:**
 
 
• **Wavelength:** In a longitudinal wave, it is the distance between two consecutive **compressions** or two consecutive **rarefactions**.
 
• **Frequency:** This refers to the **number of oscillations** per unit time. It is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• **Amplitude:** In these waves, amplitude refers to the **maximum displacement** of the particles from their mean equilibrium position.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound:** The speed of a longitudinal sound wave depends on the **density** and **elasticity** of the medium. Sound travels **fastest in solids**, followed by **liquids**, and is **slowest in gases**. For instance, the speed of sound in **steel** is approximately **5960 m/s**, while in **air** at 20 degrees Celsius, it is about **343 m/s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wave Equation:** The relationship between the **velocity (v)**, **frequency (f)**, and **wavelength (λ)** is expressed by the fundamental formula **v = f × λ**. This applies to all wave types, including longitudinal ones.
 
• **Slinky Example:** A common classroom demonstration of a longitudinal wave involves a **Slinky spring**. By pushing and pulling the end of the spring along its length, a **pulse of compression** moves down the spring, demonstrating **parallel particle motion**.
 
• **Ultrasound:** These are longitudinal waves with frequencies higher than the **upper limit of human hearing** (greater than **20,000 Hz**). They are widely used in **medical imaging** and **industrial non-destructive testing**.
 
• **Infrasound:** These are longitudinal waves with frequencies below **20 Hz**. They are often produced by large-scale natural phenomena like **volcanic eruptions** or **avalanches**.

questions.question: In household electricity supply, which of the following statements correctly describes the colour codes of the wires?

options.text: The live wire is red, the neutral wire is black, and the earth wire is green
The live wire is green, the neutral wire is red, and the earth wire is black
The live wire is blue, the neutral wire is green, and the earth wire is red
The live wire is black, the neutral wire is green, and the earth wire is blue

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The live wire is red, the neutral wire is black, and the earth wire is green**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a typical domestic electrical circuit, three separate wires are utilized to ensure the safe and functional delivery of electricity: the **live wire**, the **neutral wire**, and the **earth wire**.
 
• The **live wire** (also known as the phase wire) is traditionally color-coded **red** in **India**. This wire is at a high potential, usually **220V** relative to the ground. *Hence, the statement describing the live wire as red is correct.*
 
• The **neutral wire** is traditionally color-coded **black**. This wire completes the circuit by providing a return path for the current and is generally at **zero potential**. *Hence, the statement describing the neutral wire as black is correct.*
 
• The **earth wire** is color-coded **green** (or sometimes a combination of green and yellow in modern contexts). It is a safety wire used to connect the metallic casing of appliances to the ground. *Hence, the statement describing the earth wire as green is correct.*
 
• The standard potential difference (voltage) between the **live** and **neutral** wires in **Indian** households is **220 Volts** with a **frequency** of **50 Hz**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of the Wires:**
 
 
• **Live Wire:** It is the source of **current** coming into the house from the power station or transformer. It is the wire that carries the **voltage** and is connected to **fuses** or **Circuit Breakers (MCB)**.
 
• **Neutral Wire:** It serves as the exit point for the current, maintaining the flow of **electricity**. While it is ideally at 0V, it can carry current if the circuit is active.
 
• **Earth Wire:** It provides a low-resistance path for **leakage current**. If the insulation of the live wire fails and touches the metal body of an appliance, the current flows into the ground, preventing a fatal **electric shock** to the user.
 
 
 
• **Modern International Color Coding:**
 
 
• In recent years, many countries, including **India**, have started adopting the international standard (**IEC 60446**).
 
• In this new system, the **Live wire** is **Brown**, the **Neutral wire** is **Blue**, and the **Earth wire** remains **Green-Yellow**.
 
• However, for most traditional installations and general examinations, the **Red-Black-Green** convention remains the standard reference.
 
 
 
• **Safety Components:**
 
 
• The **Electric Fuse** is a critical safety device connected in series with the **live wire** to protect against **short-circuits** or **overloading**.
 
• A **Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB)** is a modern alternative to fuses that automatically switches off the circuit during abnormal current conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Short Circuiting:** This occurs when the **live wire** and the **neutral wire** come into direct contact due to damaged insulation, leading to a sudden, massive surge in **current** and potential **fires**.
 
• **Overloading:** This happens when too many high-power appliances (like **air conditioners**, **heaters**, and **geysers**) are connected to a single circuit, exceeding the wire's current-carrying capacity.
 
• **Safety Tip:** Switches should always be connected to the **live wire** so that when the switch is off, the appliance is completely disconnected from the high-voltage supply.
</ul

questions.question: When a drop of ink is added to water and left undisturbed, the ink gradually spreads throughout the water. Which property of matter does this observation best demonstrate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Continuous movement of particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The observation of ink spreading in water is a classic demonstration of the **continuous movement of particles** of matter. According to the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**, particles of matter are never at rest; they are in **constant, random motion**.
 
• This spontaneous intermixing of particles of two different types of matter on their own is called **diffusion**. In this case, the **ink particles** move and distribute themselves among the **water particles**.
 
• The movement happens because particles possess **Kinetic Energy**. As the ink is added, its particles collide with the water molecules, leading to a uniform distribution over time, even without stirring. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• While there are **spaces between particles**, the act of "spreading" or "traveling" throughout the liquid specifically highlights the **kinetic nature** (movement) rather than just the existence of gaps.
 
• Particles in **liquids** have enough kinetic energy to slide past one another, which allows for the fluidity and the **diffusion** process observed in the experiment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Particles of Matter:**
 
 
• Particles of matter are very small, often **beyond our imagination**.
 
• They have **spaces between them** (intermolecular spaces), which is why we can dissolve **salt** or **sugar** in water without a significant increase in volume.
 
• They **attract each other** due to **intermolecular forces**. The strength of this attraction varies from one substance to another (strongest in solids, weakest in gases).
 
• They are **continuously moving**, and this movement increases with an increase in **temperature**.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion in Different States:**
 
 
• **Gases:** Diffusion is **fastest** in gases because particles move at high speeds and have large spaces between them. An example is the smell of **perfume** or **cooking food** spreading in a room.
 
• **Liquids:** Diffusion is **slower** than in gases but faster than in solids. The spreading of **ink** or **potassium permanganate** in water are primary examples.
 
• **Solids:** Diffusion in solids is **extremely slow**. An example is **chalk marks** left on a blackboard for a long time becoming difficult to erase because particles diffuse into the surface.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Effect of Temperature:** The **rate of diffusion** is directly proportional to **temperature**. On heating, particles gain more **Kinetic Energy** and move faster, causing the ink or salt to spread more quickly in **hot water** compared to **cold water**.
 
• **Brownian Motion:** This phenomenon is closely related to the **continuous movement of particles**. It was first observed by **Robert Brown** in **1827** while looking at **pollen grains** in water. It describes the **zig-zag**, random motion of microscopic particles.
 
• **Concentration Gradient:** Diffusion always occurs from an area of **higher concentration** to an area of **lower concentration** until a **uniform distribution** (equilibrium) is reached.
 
• **Fixed Positions:** Statement 2 is incorrect because if particles had **fixed positions**, the matter would be a **rigid solid** at **absolute zero** temperature, and the ink would stay exactly where it was dropped.
 
• **Attraction Between Particles:** While **attraction** (Statement 3) exists, it actually acts against diffusion by trying to keep the particles of the same substance together. Diffusion occurs because the **kinetic energy** of the particles is sufficient to overcome some of these attractive forces.
</ul

Group terms: (sec² 18° − tan² 18°) + (cot² 18° − cosec² 18°) + sin² 30° + cosec² 60°.

Apply identities: (1) + (−1) + sin² 30° + cosec² 60°.

Value = 0 + (1/2)² + (2/√3)² = 1/4 + 4/3.

⇒ 1 + (1/2)² + (2/√3)² − 1

⇒ 1/4 + 4/3

⇒ (3 + 16) / 12

⇒ 19/12

**∴ The correct answer is 19/12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

For angles adding to 90°, ratios convert: sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot, sec ↔ cosec.

questions.question: The average of the first 16 odd natural numbers, is:

The average of the first 'n' odd natural numbers is always equal to 'n'.

Here, the total number of terms (n) = 16.

Average = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: n = 16 odd natural numbers.

Formula: Average of an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.) = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05fae30ecece86036591ed82adf705e802703b699cb2b12edd6dc99e39cc826c.png] 

⇒ First odd natural number (a) = 1

⇒ Total Sum = (n ÷ 2) × (a + l) = (16 ÷ 2) × (1 + 31) = 8 × 32 = 256

⇒ Average = Total Sum ÷ n = 256 ÷ 16 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average of Even Numbers

The average of the first n even natural numbers is always (n + 1).

Average of Consecutive Natural Numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is given by (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n odd natural numbers is n².

Average of Squares

The average of squares of first n natural numbers is [(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.</p

questions.question: In an election held between two candidates, 75% voters cast their votes. Out of them 2% votes were declared invalid. One candidate got 9261 votes which was 75% of valid votes. In this election what was the total number of registered voters ?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total number of registered voters be X.

Apply the successive percentage factors: X × (Cast%) × (Valid%) × (Candidate Share%) = 9261

⇒ X × 75/100 × 98/100 × 75/100 = 9261

⇒ X × 3/4 × 49/50 × 3/4 = 9261

⇒ X × 441/800 = 9261 ⇒ X = 21 × 800 = 16800

**∴ The correct answer is 16,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Votes cast = 75% of Registered Voters

Invalid votes = 2% of cast votes ⇒ Valid votes = 98% of cast votes

Candidate share = 75% of valid votes = 9261

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7baae72851938eef43acc71385ec573e7a53f4fb28ee29ee9bee1d56656cc042.png] 

**Formula:** Registered Voters = (Winner Votes × 100 × 100 × 100) ÷ (Cast% × Valid% × Share%)

⇒ Total Voters = (9261 × 100 × 100 × 100) ÷ (75 × 98 × 75)

⇒ Total Voters = (9261 × 4 × 50 × 4) ÷ (3 × 49 × 3)

⇒ Total Voters = (9261 × 800) ÷ (9 × 49)

⇒ Total Voters = (9261 × 800) ÷ 441

⇒ Total Voters = 21 × 800

⇒ Total Voters = 16800

**∴ The correct answer is 16,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election Vote Distribution

Total Registered = Cast + Not Cast; Cast = Valid + Invalid. Calculations are always performed on Valid votes unless specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Method

When multiple changes occur on a base value, the final value = Initial × (a/100) × (b/100) × (c/100). This is the fastest way to solve election and population problems.

Valid vs Invalid Ratio

If p% are invalid, then valid votes = Total Cast × (100 − p)/100.</p

questions.question: The difference between a single discount of 46% and two successive discounts of 30% and 20% on the marked price of an article is ₹256. Find the marked price of the article (in ₹).

Single Equivalent Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount is (x + y − xy/100)%.

questions.question: A girl goes to school at a speed of 10 km/hr. She comes back with a speed of 40 km/hr. Find her average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance is the same for both journeys, use the Harmonic Mean formula:

Average Speed = (2 × s₁ × s₂) / (s₁ + s₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 10 × 40) / (10 + 40)

⇒ Average Speed = 800 / 50 = 16 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed while going (s₁) = 10 km/hr

Speed while returning (s₂) = 40 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f9a7aa8de508f4c0ca3a3f3cae2e9be386a8f04c0e36f106d6c9ac3b437cf42.png] 

Let the distance between home and school be the LCM of 10 and 40, which is 40 km.

⇒ Distance (D) = 40 km

⇒ Time taken while going (t₁) = Distance / s₁ = 40 / 10 = 4 hours

⇒ Time taken while returning (t₂) = Distance / s₂ = 40 / 40 = 1 hour

⇒ Total Distance = 40 + 40 = 80 km

⇒ Total Time = 4 + 1 = 5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 80 / 5 = 16 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for different distances

questions.question: If 66% of the first number is equal to three-fifths of the second number, what is the ratio of the first number to the second number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert both values to a common form (percentage).

66% of 1st Number = (3/5 × 100)% of 2ⁿd Number

66% of 1st Number = 60% of 2ⁿd Number

Ratio (1st : 2ⁿd) = Inverse of their coefficients = 60 : 66

Simplifying by dividing by 6 ⇒ 10 : 11

**∴ The correct answer is 10 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of first number = 66%

Fraction of second number = 3/5

**Formula:**

Value = (Percentage/100) × Number | Ratio A : B = A/B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cece5c0902999727f7d3fa39a8f0b278da678aac69b68ac6f06c91c356f59594.png] 

Let the first number be x and the second number be y.

⇒ 66% of x = (3/5) of y

⇒ (66/100) × x = (3/5) × y

⇒ (33/50) × x = (3/5) × y

⇒ x/y = (3/5) ÷ (33/50)

⇒ x/y = (3/5) × (50/33)

⇒ x/y = (1 × 10) / (1 × 11)

⇒ x/y = 10/11

**∴ The correct answer is 10 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert x% to a fraction, divide by 100: x/100. Conversely, multiply a fraction by 100 to get the percentage.

Ratio Balancing Rule

If m × A = n × B, then the ratio A : B is equal to n : m. This is known as the inverse coefficient rule.

Simplifying Ratios

A ratio a : b can be simplified by dividing both terms by their Highest Common Factor (HCF) to reach the simplest form.</p

questions.question: The ratio of incomes of two persons is 8:5 and the ratio of their expenditure is 2:1. If each of them manages to save ₹160 per month, find the difference of their monthly income.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income ratio = 8 : 5 and Expenditure ratio = 2 : 1

Savings are same (₹160), use cross-product method:

| (8 × 1) − (5 × 2) | units = | 160 × (1 − 2) |

⇒ | 8 − 10 | units = | −160 | ⇒ 2 units = 160

⇒ 1 unit = 80

Difference in income = (8 − 5) = 3 units = 3 × 80 = ₹240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Ratio of Incomes = 8 : 5, Ratio of Expenditures = 2 : 1, Individual Savings = ₹160.

Formula: Income − Expenditure = Savings

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55b4ef4a6ccce424c9f010589935ca1f6304f1dd8918a7333e3180879253204b.png] 

Let the incomes be 8x and 5x.

Let the expenditures be 2y and y.

⇒ 8x − 2y = 160 ... (i)

⇒ 5x − y = 160 ⇒ y = 5x − 160 ... (ii)

Substituting the value of y from equation (ii) into equation (i):

⇒ 8x − 2(5x − 160) = 160

⇒ 8x − 10x + 320 = 160

⇒ −2x = 160 − 320

⇒ −2x = −160 ⇒ x = 80

⇒ Monthly income of first person = 8 × 80 = ₹640

⇒ Monthly income of second person = 5 × 80 = ₹400

⇒ Difference = 640 − 400 = ₹240

**∴ The correct answer is ₹240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings

The basic relationship is Income = Expenditure + Savings. If savings are equal for both parties, the difference in income units is proportional to the difference in expenditure units after scaling.

Ratio Balancing

To solve without algebra, multiply the expenditure ratio by a factor so that the difference (Income Unit − Expenditure Unit) is equal for both persons.

Proportion Rule

If A:B is the ratio of two quantities, the difference is expressed as |A − B| units. To find the real value, multiply this unit difference by the value of 1 unit.

questions.question: Find the volume of a cuboid whose length, breadth and height are in the ratio 4 : 3 : 2 and total surface area is 832 {cm}² .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) ratio units = 2 × (4×3 + 3×2 + 2×4) = 52 units²

Scaling factor squared (x²) = Total Area ÷ Ratio units = 832 ÷ 52 = 16

Linear scaling factor (x) = √16 = 4 cm

Volume ratio units = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 units³

Actual Volume = 24 × (x)³ = 24 × 4³ = 24 × 64 = 1536 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1536 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of length (L) : breadth (B) : height (H) = 4 : 3 : 2

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 832 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of cuboid = 2(LB + BH + HL)

Volume of cuboid = L × B × H

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bfbae3992048eb5c0eeda1f36d1ebcc94e2f6d7acb585a44bcf1a5d5da24178e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Length (L) = 4x, Breadth (B) = 3x, and Height (H) = 2x

⇒ 2[(4x × 3x) + (3x × 2x) + (2x × 4x)] = 832

⇒ 2[12x² + 6x² + 8x²] = 832

⇒ 2[26x²] = 832

⇒ 52x² = 832

⇒ x² = 832 ÷ 52 = 16

⇒ x = √16 = 4

⇒ L = 4 × 4 = 16 cm

⇒ B = 3 × 4 = 12 cm

⇒ H = 2 × 4 = 8 cm

⇒ Volume = 16 × 12 × 8

⇒ Volume = 1536 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1536 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The surface area of the four vertical walls of the cuboid is 2h(l + b).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can fit in a cuboid is √(l² + b² + h²).

Properties of a Cube

A cube is a special cuboid where l = b = h = a. TSA = 6a² and Volume = a³.</p

questions.question: Nine years ago, Asha was thrice as old as Bhawna. Seven years from now, Asha will be twice as old as Bhawna. Find the present age of Bhawna.
questions.solution:

Ratio (A : B) 9 yrs ago = 3 : 1 (Difference = 2)

Ratio (A : B) 7 yrs hence = 2 : 1 × 2 = 4 : 2 (Difference = 2)

Total time gap = 9 + 7 = 16 years

Unit difference in B’s ratio = 2 − 1 = 1 unit

⇒ 1 unit = 16 years

Bhawna’s age 9 yrs ago = 1 unit = 16 years

Bhawna’s present age = 16 + 9 = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

Given: 9 years ago Asha = 3 × Bhawna. 7 years hence Asha = 2 × Bhawna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c60dcdaba912d47728ee4e53113b62ebfe304b662ed53fc6981310a64c174df.png] 

Let the present age of Bhawna be B and Asha be A.

⇒ (A − 9) = 3(B − 9)

⇒ A − 9 = 3B − 27

⇒ A = 3B − 18 — (i)

⇒ (A + 7) = 2(B + 7)

⇒ A + 7 = 2B + 14

⇒ A = 2B + 7 — (ii)

Equating (i) and (ii):

⇒ 3B − 18 = 2B + 7

⇒ 3B − 2B = 7 + 18

⇒ B = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals always remains the same, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Balancing

In age problems involving ratios, multiply the ratios by the difference of the other ratio to equalize the unit gaps between years.

If the average age of a group of n people is X, then after k years, the new average age will be X + k.</p

questions.question: There are 156 boy students and 143 girl students in a school. The principal wants to divide them in sections, such that a section can have only boys or only girls. If all sections should have the same number of students, and the principal wants to have as fewer sections as possible, how many sections would be there in the school?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To minimize sections, maximize students per section using HCF.

Students per section = HCF(156, 143)

156 = 13 × 12 and 143 = 13 × 11 ⇒ HCF = 13

Number of sections = (156 ÷ 13) + (143 ÷ 13)

Number of sections = 12 + 11 = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of boy students = 156

Number of girl students = 143

Condition: Each section must have same number of students and contain only boys or girls.

**Formula Used:**

To have the fewest sections, the size of each section must be the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the number of boys and girls.

Total Sections = (Number of Boys ÷ HCF) + (Number of Girls ÷ HCF)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b7e7fcdaaa7e66b43de2d43f2c30f9e5b90390855a9113835e9f4f661d6b629.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 156 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 13

⇒ Prime factors of 143 = 11 × 13

⇒ Common factor (HCF) = 13

⇒ Number of boy sections = 156 ÷ 13 = 12

⇒ Number of girl sections = 143 ÷ 13 = 11

⇒ Total number of sections = 12 + 11

⇒ Total sections = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

It is the largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without a remainder. It is used to find the maximum size for equal grouping.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

LCM is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by both a and b. It is used for problems involving cycles or meeting times.

HCF × LCM Property

For two numbers a and b, Product of numbers = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).</p

questions.question: Find the single discount equivalent to two successive discounts of 28% and 16%.

questions.question: Successive discounts of 40% and 15% are equivalent to a single discount of ________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Discount Formula for two successive discounts a% and b%:

Net Discount = [a + b − (a × b / 100)]%

Here, a = 40 and b = 15

Net Discount = [40 + 15 − (40 × 15 / 100)]% = [55 − 6]% = 49%

**∴ The correct answer is 49%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

First discount (d₁) = 40%

Second discount (d₂) = 15%

Formula: Final Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd59ab0241f6614371a984aa9cf919ead5e02b1e94dbc624ae0dc88504d6233e.png] 

Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100 units.

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 100 − (40% of 100)

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 100 − 40 = 60 units

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 60 − (15% of 60)

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 60 − (15/100 × 60)

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 60 − 9 = 51 units

⇒ Single Equivalent Discount = (MP − Final Price) / MP × 100

⇒ Single Equivalent Discount = (100 − 51) / 100 × 100

⇒ Single Equivalent Discount = 49%

**∴ The correct answer is 49%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Three Successive Discounts

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, calculate the net of a and b first, then use that result with c using the formula x + y − xy/100.

Marked Price and Selling Price Relation

Selling Price = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100. This is useful for large number calculations.

Successive Percentage Increase

If values increase successively, use the formula: a + b + (ab / 100)% for the overall percentage change.</p

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 36^circ and angle B = 93^circ . The bisectors of angle C and angle D meet at O. What is the measure of angle DOC ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle between bisectors of ∠C and ∠D in a quadrilateral = (∠A + ∠B) ÷ 2

Given: ∠A = 36° and ∠B = 93°

∠DOC = (36° + 93°) ÷ 2

∠DOC = 129° ÷ 2 = 64.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 64.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: ∠A = 36°, ∠B = 93°, CO and DO are bisectors of ∠C and ∠D.

Formula: Sum of angles in a quadrilateral = 360° | Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a96a7e9a7ef13da55e1b9aaf0d42bba9aeb9c1ca739d42364f1418dd5b0cf72.png] 

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 36° + 93° + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 129° + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ ∠C + ∠D = 360° − 129° = 231°

⇒ Divide by 2: (∠C + ∠D) / 2 = 231° / 2 = 115.5°

⇒ In ΔDOC, ∠DOC + ∠OCD + ∠ODC = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + (∠C / 2) + (∠D / 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + 115.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC = 180° − 115.5° = 64.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 64.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

For any n-sided polygon, the sum of interior angles is (n − 2) × 180°.

Angle Bisector Relation

In a quadrilateral, the angle between the internal bisectors of two opposite angles is half the difference of the other two angles.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, meaning their sum is always 180°.</p

questions.question: The number of two-digit numbers divisible by 6 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Smallest two-digit multiple of 6 = 12

Largest two-digit multiple of 6 = 96

Total numbers (n) = [(Last Term − First Term) ÷ Common Difference] + 1

Total numbers (n) = [(96 − 12) ÷ 6] + 1

n = [84 ÷ 6] + 1 = 14 + 1 = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Two-digit numbers range from 10 to 99. We need to find multiples of 6 in this range.

Formula used: nth term of an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.), aₙ = a + (n − 1)d

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c69b9e1d4d3b2b2e7d18e751c5531790d6be0ea51adca50d8f2f9c1b35056e5e.png] 

⇒ First term (a) = 12

⇒ Last term (aₙ) = 96

⇒ Common difference (d) = 6

⇒ 96 = 12 + (n − 1) × 6

⇒ 96 − 12 = (n − 1) × 6

⇒ 84 = (n − 1) × 6

⇒ n − 1 = 84 ÷ 6

⇒ n − 1 = 14

⇒ n = 14 + 1 = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence of numbers where the difference between consecutive terms is constant, denoted as 'd'.

Sum of n terms of AP

The sum Sₙ can be calculated using Sₙ = (n ÷ 2)[2a + (n − 1)d] or Sₙ = (n ÷ 2)[a + l].

Divisibility Rule of 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by both 2 (ends in even digit) and 3 (sum of digits is divisible by 3).</p

questions.question: A man loses 20% of his money. He then spends 25% of what remains. If he is left with ₹525, what was his original amount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total remaining fraction = (1 − 1/5) × (1 − 1/4) = 4/5 × 3/4 = 3/5

Here, 3 units represent the remaining amount ₹525.

1 unit = 525 ÷ 3 = 175

Original amount (5 units) = 175 × 5 = ₹875

**∴ The correct answer is ₹875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss percentage = 20%

Expenditure from remainder = 25%

Final amount left = ₹525

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (100 − R₁)/100 × (100 − R₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b8c55559993e05d6c2eab4c1f644afe904f0c1636b547259a46098e5fe2be86.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount spent from remainder = 25% of 0.8x = (25/100) × 0.8x = 0.2x

⇒ Final amount left = 0.8x − 0.2x = 0.6x

⇒ 0.6x = 525

⇒ x = 525 ÷ 0.6

⇒ x = 5250 ÷ 6

⇒ x = 875

**∴ The correct answer is ₹875.**

questions.question: If the ratio of the the speeds of three cars is 2:3:5, then the ratio of the time taken by these three cars to travel the same distance is:

When distance is constant, the ratio of time is the inverse of the ratio of speed.

Ratio of speeds = 2 : 3 : 5

Ratio of times = 15 : 10 : 6

Ratio of speeds of three cars (S₁ : S₂ : S₃) = 2 : 3 : 5

⇒ LCM(2, 3, 5) = 30

⇒ T₁ : T₂ : T₃ = (1/2 × 30) : (1/3 × 30) : (1/5 × 30)

⇒ T₁ : T₂ : T₃ = 15 : 10 : 6

**∴ The correct answer is 15 : 10 : 6.**

• The primary focus of this study is to identify **biological markers (biomarkers)** that correlate with **healthy brain aging** and to understand how certain individuals remain resilient against cognitive decline despite various adversities.
 
• It is a **longitudinal study**, meaning it tracks the same group of individuals over an extended period to observe changes in **cognitive health**, **brain structure**, and **lifestyle factors**.
 
• The initiative aims to address the growing challenge of **neurodegenerative disorders** such as **Alzheimer’s disease** and **dementia** within the specific context of the **Indian population**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 1.***

• **Target Demographic:** 
 
 
• The **BHARAT study** typically recruits participants aged **45 years and above** to capture the early transitions into the aging phase.
 
• This demographic is critical because **pathological changes** in the brain often begin decades before **clinical symptoms** of dementia appear.
